clue.text: Quirky character — maybe resents snag being found

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of these two words could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resentful at hitting a snag is said to show an odd personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals that RESENTS and SNAG are rearranged together; 'being found' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangeness is the quality of being odd or peculiar, a quirky nature.

clue.text: A pear is the product of such blossom

indicators.note: what is produced from these words is a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A gardener muses that a pear grows from a particular kind of flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the product of' tells you to rearrange A PEAR IS; the surface pretends the pear is the fruit of the blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiraea is a shrub of the rose family grown for its sprays of small flowers.

clue.text: Carry off, lock stock and barrel

definitions.meaning: to carry off is to plunder or ransack
the firing mechanism, wooden butt and tube are the three main parts of a gun

explanation.walkthrough: 'lock, stock and barrel' usually means 'entirely', but here it literally lists the parts of a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to ransack and steal, and a rifle is a long gun made of lock, stock and barrel.

clue.text: Persons considering themselves barely acceptable

parts.note: 'barely' means scarcely, but read literally it means unclothed: people who think being bare is fine

explanation.walkthrough: 'barely acceptable' reads as 'only just tolerable', but the setter means people who find it acceptable to go bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists hold that going about without clothes is perfectly proper.

clue.text: Voice from the crowd

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or from, as in ex-works
a press is a dense crowd or throng of people

explanation.surface: A single shout rises out of a throng of spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to put it into words, to state it.

clue.text: The demand for dues from confounded taxmen etc

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grumble about tax collectors and their demands for payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' looks like an angry adjective for the taxmen but signals the rearrangement of TAXMEN ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is a forcible demand for payment, a rare form of which is this word.

clue.text: Cut out by design

parts.note: read as a sheet with a pattern cut out of it so that a design can be painted through

explanation.walkthrough: 'by design' suggests 'deliberately', but here it means a template with a pattern cut into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a thin sheet with holes cut in a pattern, used to reproduce it with paint or ink.

clue.text: Expressed disdain when so inspired

definitions.meaning: a contemptuous snort through the nose shows scorn
inspired literally means breathed in, here through the nose

explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired' is used in its literal sense of breathing in, not of being creatively moved.
explanation.definitionFit: A disdainful snort and a short inhalation through the nostrils are both this action.

clue.text: Awfully erratic set, a lot of white-collar workers

indicators.note: awfully suggests badly put together, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Office staff are dismissed as an unreliable bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' signals a rearrangement of ERRATIC SET plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretariat is the administrative office staff of an organisation, a body of clerical employees.

clue.text: The sort of horses which are later described in an extra note

indicators.note: described means drawn around, so the word later is enclosed by another piece

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added to the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A racing tipster notes in a postscript which horses will run in a later race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described in' means 'drawn round', the geometric sense. Platers are low-grade British racehorses that run in minor 'plate' races.
explanation.definitionFit: A plater is a modest racehorse that competes mainly in plate races of lower quality.

clue.text: Broke with following in very short time…

parts.note: broke as in broke apart means split
second means coming next in order, following

explanation.surface: Someone parted company and soon came after, all in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue, which refers back to this one.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is an instant, the briefest moment.

clue.text: A girl left in custody

indicators.note: in means the letter for left sits within the word for custody

parts.note: care means guardianship or custody, as in a child in care

explanation.surface: A young woman has been abandoned in police custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare is a female first name.

clue.text: Not at all keen to give credit

definitions.text: Not at all keen to give credit

parts.words: Not at all keen to give credit
parts.note: read as being reluctant to believe something rather than a lender reluctant to lend

explanation.walkthrough: 'give credit' sounds financial, like a bank refusing a loan, but means 'believe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubting person is slow to accept claims as true.

clue.text: A scholar returning mathematical work behind time

indicators.note: behind means the reversed work comes after the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: returning means the word for the calculations is read backwards

parts.note: sums are arithmetic exercises

explanation.surface: An academic is going back over some old calculations late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SUMS into SMUS, which goes 'behind' ERA. Erasmus was the Dutch Renaissance humanist scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the leading humanist scholar of the Northern Renaissance.

clue.text: …and after that there's nothing America finds crucial

indicators.note: after means the next pieces follow the word referred to

parts.note: that points back to the very short time of the previous clue, a brief instant
O looks like zero, nothing
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Continuing the story: a nation finds there is nothing left at the decisive point.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis ties this to 9 Down: 'that' stands for its 'very short time', and 'after' puts the rest behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A momentous event is of great importance, decisive in its consequences.

clue.text: Letters about fish

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of the word are mixed

explanation.surface: Correspondence concerning seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals rearranging LETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The sterlet is a small sturgeon of Eurasian rivers, prized for its caviar.

clue.text: Thrown into a panic, a trainee prepared to do battle

parts.note: L, for learner, is shown on plates of a trainee driver
armed means carrying weapons, ready to fight

explanation.surface: A nervous recruit given weapons for the fight is terrified.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alarmed is suddenly frightened or anxious.

clue.text: Old jar containing some camphor and other oils

indicators.note: these words contain some of their letters as the answer, running across the word break

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel holds a little camphor and other aromatic oils.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'camphor' and 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage vessel.

clue.text: The right to be in several clubs

indicators.note: to be in means the abbreviation for right is put inside the word for several

parts.note: divers is an old word meaning several or sundry

explanation.surface: A claim to membership of various clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVERS is an archaic adjective meaning 'various, several'. 'clubs' looks like societies but means golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers are golf clubs used for long shots off the tee.

clue.text: Struggle to get to the top of a crater possibly

definitions.text: Struggle to get to the top

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of the words might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Climbers scramble up the rim of a volcanic crater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals rearranging A CRATER.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the fierce competition for success in working life.

clue.text: Artillerymen with gun to bring up — it's routine

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up means the combined pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: Gunners hauling a weapon up the hill as part of their drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring up' reverses RA and LUGER together, giving REGUL+AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means usual and habitual, done as a matter of course.

clue.text: Mean to issue a statement before very long

indicators.note: before means the word for stating comes ahead of the word for a long time

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert
an age, as in 'it took ages', is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone intends to make a declaration soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' poses as 'intend' but is the arithmetic mean.
explanation.definitionFit: An average is a mean value, the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: Death — following a wicked creature's threatening

indicators.note: following means the word for death comes after the creature

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
an ending, the end of life, is death

explanation.surface: A dark tale: death comes on the heels of a demon's menace.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impending is about to happen, looming like a threat.

clue.text: Belief stated, the leftist is in business!

indicators.note: is in means the word for a leftist sits inside the business abbreviation

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business
a Red is a communist or socialist

explanation.surface: A declaration that a left-winger has gone into commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: A swimmer set about exercise and did well

indicators.note: set about means the fish is placed around the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: a cod is a fish, a swimmer
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A fish took up exercise and thrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage successfully in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Couple given book about swine making comeback

indicators.note: about means the large volume is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word for the pig is reversed

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pair are given a volume on pigs making a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns the pig round before the book goes 'about' it; 'given' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people together.

clue.text: Country boy enclosing a plot

indicators.note: enclosing means the boy surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a plan is a plot or scheme

explanation.surface: A rural lad fences in a patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective with 'boy', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is a region of northern Scandinavia, home of the Sami.

clue.text: Euclid's proposition for fools' game

parts.note: asses are fools
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A theorem of Euclid serves as a pastime for idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pons asinorum' is Euclid's fifth proposition, that the base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, said to sort the slow from the able.
explanation.definitionFit: The pons asinorum is the traditional name for an early theorem in Euclid's Elements.
